clue.text: Nuts in AA to meet separately

indicators.note: someone nuts has lost all order in their head, and letters described that way will not stay in the sequence they are given

blocks.note: every letter of these four words goes into the mix exactly as it stands

explanation.walkthrough: AA is a support group on the surface and just two letters in the wordplay, and 'Nuts' has to be read as the state the letters are in rather than as the people in the room.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing things one at a time is doing them separately rather than all at once, so the phrase works as an adverb of manner.

clue.text: Female no wife for Saudi neighbour

indicators.note: 'no wife' announces that the wife is absent, so the letter standing for her is not there to be written

blocks.note: a female is a woman
W is the crossword's standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.walkthrough: Crossword shorthand does all the work here, and W for wife is worth memorising: the surface reads as a description of one person, never as an instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Oman shares a long desert border with Saudi Arabia, so it is literally one of the kingdom's neighbours on the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: American visiting The Ritz all obey — volatile player?

indicators.note: a visitor arrives among the people already there, so this letter joins the others rather than standing apart from them
a volatile substance will not sit still in the state you found it, and neither will this handful of letters

blocks.note: A is the standard abbreviation for American
all four words are raw material, letter for letter

explanation.walkthrough: The Ritz and a well-behaved crowd make a nice picture and are doing nothing but supplying letters. The question mark admits that one actress is only an example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A player is anyone who acts a part, and Elizabeth Taylor was one of Hollywood's great screen actresses — an example of the class, not a synonym.

clue.text: Hint from artist forsaking daily grind

indicators.note: to forsake something is to walk out on it for good, so those two letters quit the phrase and do not come back

blocks.note: the rat race is the daily grind of commuting and the office
RA is a Royal Academician, the crossword's standard artist

explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily grind' has to be heard as the idiom rather than as a charwoman's work, and RA is worth banking: it is the artist in a great many clues.
explanation.definitionFit: A trace of something is the faintest sign that it was ever there, which is what a hint amounts to when nobody says anything outright.

clue.text: Garments: those in which to sleep almost removed?

indicators.note: something removed is taken out and carried off, so that block of letters is lifted clean out of the longer word

blocks.note: nightshirts are what you sleep in
nigh means almost, as in 'the end is nigh'

explanation.walkthrough: The colon does the misdirecting: it makes 'those in which to sleep' look like a second description of the answer when it is really the word being cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: T-shirts are the plain short-sleeved cotton tops named for their outline, so 'garments' is the general word for one particular kind.

clue.text: Overcome small albatross sometimes seen here?

blocks.note: to master a fear is to overcome it
S is the size printed on a clothing label

explanation.walkthrough: Two golf words do the misdirecting: an albatross is a seabird until you remember it is also three under par on a single hole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masters is the Augusta major, so it is one of the few places a golfing albatross is ever likely to be witnessed.

clue.text: Snake-haired monster leaving cheese for writer

indicators.note: once someone has left a room they are no longer in it, so those letters walk out of the word that held them

blocks.note: gorgonzola is the blue Italian cheese
the Gorgons of myth, Medusa among them, had snakes for hair

explanation.walkthrough: The cheese is named after the Italian town of Gorgonzola, and the coincidence the setter has spotted is that a Greek monster sits in the front of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Émile Zola was the French novelist of Germinal and the open letter 'J'accuse', so 'writer' names him by his trade.

clue.text: One possibly retired hurt alongside opener?

indicators.note: a hurt limb has been knocked out of its proper shape, and these letters are knocked out of theirs

blocks.note: the two words supply every letter, exactly as they are written

explanation.walkthrough: The cricket is a decoy from end to end — retired hurt, an opener, a fielder alongside — and none of it does anything but hand over letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-age pensioner has reached the age of drawing a state pension, and 'possibly' allows for the retired people who are nothing of the kind.

clue.text: Significant hole in one by an old African?

blocks.note: an abyss is a chasm too deep to see the bottom of
the little word is written in as it stands
I is the Roman numeral for one
the indefinite article comes across unchanged

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hole in one' is a golfer's phrase on the surface and three separate pieces underneath, which is where this clue hides its seams.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia was the name Ethiopia went by until the twentieth century, so an Abyssinian is what an Ethiopian used to be called.

clue.text: Caribbean sort to sight whaler up north

indicators.note: this is a down entry, so 'up' asks you to read those letters from the foot of the column back to the top

blocks.note: to sight a target is to aim at it
Captain Ahab is the whaler hunting Moby-Dick
N is the compass abbreviation for north

explanation.walkthrough: Ahab is the crossword's whaler and worth remembering. The compass point stays the right way round because it is added after the turn rather than before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A Bahamian is a native of the Bahamas, an island nation in the Caribbean, so 'sort' is asking for a person and not a place.

clue.text: Andy Burnham is cross about a Liberal raising stock

indicators.note: to cross two breeds is to mix them together into something new, and these letters are interbred the same way
'about' scatters the extra letters in among the rest instead of leaving them in a block at one end

blocks.note: the mayor's name and the verb after it all go into the mix
the article counts as one more letter
L is the standard abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.walkthrough: Andy Burnham is the mayor of Greater Manchester, and reading 'cross' as angry rather than as interbreeding is what keeps the sentence sounding like politics.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal husbandry is the farming business of breeding and rearing livestock, and 'stock' is the farmer's own word for a herd.

clue.text: 50 with a king by unearthly American feature

blocks.note: L is fifty in Roman numerals
the article is taken as read
K is the king on a chessboard and on a playing card
eerie is the everyday word for unearthly

explanation.walkthrough: Roman fifty and the chess king are two single letters worth banking, and the surface's hint of a ghost story is there only to make 'unearthly' look like scene-setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Erie is one of the five Great Lakes on the border between the United States and Canada, so 'feature' names it as geography.

clue.text: Protection from serviceman in ebbing tide

indicators.note: 'in' puts the soldier inside the other word rather than alongside it
an ebbing tide is running back out the way it came in, so its letters run the other way too

blocks.note: the tide is the sea, in the poets' sense of the word
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.walkthrough: The whole picture — a serviceman, a beach, the water going out — is built to keep you thinking about a landing rather than about Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The aegis was the shield Zeus lent Athena, and to be under someone's aegis is still to be under their protection.

clue.text: Ground where one welcomes island leader

indicators.note: grain that has been ground comes out as loose meal with no shape left to it, and so do these letters
to welcome somebody is to take them in, so the short abbreviation joins the letters already gathered

blocks.note: both words go into the mix exactly as they stand
Is. is the map-maker's abbreviation for island

explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' looks like a noun — a piece of land — right up to the moment you need it as the past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Dwight D. Eisenhower commanded the Allied armies in Europe and then served two terms as US president, so 'leader' names him by his job.

clue.text: Pole features in Room 101 making comeback

indicators.note: a comeback brings someone back the way they went, so the assembled letters return in reverse

blocks.note: room in the sense of space, as in room to move
CI is 101 in Roman numerals

explanation.walkthrough: Room 101 belongs to Orwell on the surface, where nobody reads the number as arithmetic — which is exactly what the wordplay needs you to do.
explanation.definitionFit: The polar ice caps are the permanent sheets of ice covering the Arctic and the Antarctic, so they are the features of both poles.

clue.text: One kills when elite troops stray from path

blocks.note: 'as' and 'when' swap freely: as I arrived, when I arrived
the SAS is the British army's special forces regiment
to sin is to stray from the straight and narrow

explanation.walkthrough: The military surface does the hiding: 'stray from path' looks like a manoeuvre going wrong when it is really a churchman's word.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is one who kills by stealth, for hire or for politics, so the clue's bare 'one kills' is the whole trade.

clue.text: Slippery surface sends child into bridge

indicators.note: to send a thing somewhere is to put it there, and the clue names the destination immediately afterwards
'into' means ending up inside something rather than merely beside it, so one word finishes in the middle of the other

blocks.note: a span is the reach of a bridge, and the bridge itself
a kid is a child

explanation.walkthrough: Nothing here looks like an instruction, which is the trick: 'sends... into' is an ordinary piece of English doing a container's job.
explanation.definitionFit: A skid pan is the deliberately slippery yard where drivers are taught to control a skid, so it is a surface built to lose grip.

clue.text: Wild sheep accompanies us in ancient city

indicators.note: wild means untamed and unordered, so the letters will not stay in the tidy line the clue lends them
one thing that accompanies another walks along beside it, so these two letters sit next to the rest and not inside them

blocks.note: the five letters of SHEEP resettled into a new order
the pronoun is written in as it stands

explanation.walkthrough: A wild sheep is a real animal — a mouflon — which is why the phrase reads as description rather than as an instruction to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephesus was the great Greek and Roman city on the coast of what is now Turkey, famous for its temple of Artemis.

clue.text: Is it Ringo installing Ringoe as PM?

indicators.note: to install a part is to fit it inside the housing, so the shorter piece goes into the middle of the longer

blocks.note: Ringo Starr, the Beatles' drummer
Ringoe sets this puzzle, and a setter referring to themselves is ME

explanation.walkthrough: A setter writing 'me' about themselves is a standing convention, and here the name that does it is one letter away from a Beatle's.
explanation.definitionFit: PM is the everyday shorthand for prime minister, the office Sir Keir Starmer took for Labour in 2024.

clue.text: Granny seen in Dickens a godsend

indicators.note: what is seen in something is inside it, so these letters show through from within the words around them

blocks.note: Boz is the name Dickens signed his early sketches with
the article joins on as it stands
nan is what a great many children call their grandmother

explanation.walkthrough: The affectionate-sounding 'Granny seen in Dickens' is a plain instruction once you know Boz, and 'a godsend' has to give up its article to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A bonanza is a sudden run of riches or good luck, which is what a godsend is when it turns up unasked for.

clue.text: Assist insect outside close to sunken well

indicators.note: standing outside something means going round it, so the insect wraps around the single letter
the close of a word is where it stops, so only its final letter is wanted

blocks.note: the bee is the crossword's default insect
the letter that closes the word sunken
someone fit and well is in good health

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' is the pivot: it reads as part of 'sunken well' in the surface and as a word for healthy in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To benefit someone is to do them good, the same helping hand 'assist' names, though benefit can be a noun as well.

clue.text: Captains perhaps in privy at sea

blocks.note: the head of a body or a business is its chief, and a captain is one kind of chief
the traditional name for a ship's lavatory, found forward near the bow in the age of sail

explanation.walkthrough: The seam is hidden by 'in', which joins the two halves so smoothly that the sentence reads as one picture of officers in a ship's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an organisation is its chief, so captains are heads; and a ship's lavatory has been called the heads since the age of sail.

clue.text: Sceptical as a good number remain we hear

indicators.note: 'we hear' asks for the sound of a word and not its spelling, so the letters follow the ear

blocks.note: the article is taken as read
G is the standard abbreviation for good
no. is the everyday abbreviation for number
to stick is to remain, and STICK said aloud is what these four letters spell out

explanation.walkthrough: Three of the four pieces are abbreviations you can bank, and the last one only works if you say it: STIC is no word at all, but it sounds like one.
explanation.definitionFit: An agnostic holds that nothing can be known either way about God, which is exactly the doubting position 'sceptical' describes.

clue.text: Seconds for good child

blocks.note: s is the abbreviation for seconds on any stopwatch
pro means in favour of, which is to say for
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.walkthrough: Every word before the definition stands for something shorter, and 'for' is the surprise: it is not joining the pieces, it is one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Sprog is British services slang for a small child, the half-affectionate word a parent might use about a new baby.

clue.text: Revolutionary augury one found in movie?

indicators.note: a revolution turns a thing right round, so the letters come out facing the other way

blocks.note: an augury is an omen, a sign of what is coming

explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke as well as a definition, since the whole plot of the film is the search that the title promises will succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: Nemo is the lost clownfish whose recovery gives the Pixar film its title, so the definition names one example rather than a class.

clue.text: Ruler's order for backer briefly touring two states

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short, so the last letter of this one never gets written
a tour goes all the way round a place rather than past it, so these letters end up wrapped around what they visit

blocks.note: a will is the order somebody leaves for what must happen
IA is Iowa and MO Missouri, two postal abbreviations
the little word is written straight in, letter for letter
an angel is the backer who puts money into a show, docked of its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is the join, and everything after it is machinery: an angel here is theatre money rather than a cherub, and the states are pure postcode.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Orange took the English throne as William III in 1689, so 'ruler' names him by the office rather than the man.

clue.text: Exquisite morsel missed in savoury dish

indicators.note: what is missed is not there when you look for it, so those three letters are absent from the dish

blocks.note: a rarebit is the cheese-on-toast savoury
a bit is a small morsel of something

explanation.walkthrough: A Welsh rarebit is cheese on toast and nothing to do with rabbit, and the clue's 'morsel' is the very piece of it that has to go.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare talent is an exquisite one — the sense of rare that means outstanding, not the one that means seldom found.

clue.text: Star to rage when drunk grabs dress

indicators.note: a drunk cannot walk a straight line, and these letters will not keep to theirs either
to grab something is to close your hand round it, so the letters shut around what they take hold of

blocks.note: the six letters of TO RAGE resettled into a new order
garb is what you dress in — clothing

explanation.walkthrough: 'Star' is the definition and the joke at once: the wordplay has a screen legend raging drunk and grabbing at a frock.
explanation.definitionFit: Greta Garbo was the Swedish actress of Grand Hotel and Ninotchka, so 'star' names one of the biggest names in Hollywood.
